about: Custom Aftermarket Car Center Console Upgrade - measured reference from my iPhone 14 Pro LiDAR scan (Scaniverse, mesh mode, 3 Oct 12:45), aligned to the shared model frame; dimensions approximate.

frame.origin: middle of the notch back edge (stitch line where the flat deck meets the rolled lip) on the deck top
frame.handedness: The shared frame (x passenger, y rear, z up) is left-handed. STL files use these numbers directly (like the OpenSCAD STLs), so in a right-handed viewer they look mirrored, exactly like the SCAD parts; assemble.py's y-flip fixes both. The GLB files are already in Blender metres with assemble.py's convention: Blender (X,Y,Z) = (x/1000, -y/1000, z/1000), i.e. they overlay the assembled parts directly and are not mirrored.

files.panel_glb: panel_scan_modelframe.glb (textured, Blender metres, assemble.py convention; clock dial centre blurred in the texture)

transforms.note: raw = coordinates after Blender's default glTF import of scan_01_12-45.glb (metres, Z up). Apply to column vectors [x,y,z,1]. det < 0 for the model-frame matrix (mirror).

table_plane.method: RANSAC on the whole scene, then a robust least-squares refit on table points 30-200 mm around the panel footprint
table_plane.note: wooden table is not perfectly flat (whole-table rms 1.4 mm on inliers, some areas 8-16 mm off)

table_plane_in_model_frame.note: 120.0 mm below the deck at the origin; 0.26 deg roll and 0.42 deg pitch relative to the deck plane

deck_plane.method: RANSAC + least squares on up-facing panel points 105-135 mm above the table

centre_line.method: mirror-symmetry search on the top-view outline, refined by fitting the midline of the two deck seams (z = 2 mm contour) over y = 0..230
centre_line.note: the free arms are not symmetric (passenger arm splays ~5-10 mm more); the rigid deck was used

stitch_line.method: dark crease in the texture across the notch back (brightness minimum), where the surface is ~1.5 mm below the deck plane; flat deck (z > -2) starts at y = 0 +/- 1

scale_check.summary: No consistent scale error: large dimensions agree with the tape to within -1.3 % .. +1.7 % (mean about -0.3 %). No scale correction applied.

notch.note: open edge = innermost deck-level geometry (z > -12). Notch widens forward: ~8.5 deg per side from y=-25 to -105, ~14 deg from -105 to -185.

arms.outline_note: per-y outer x, band-top x and notch (inner) x are in widths_every_10mm and notch.side_edges_by_y; the flat strip beside the notch sinks below the deck plane forward (about -2 at y=-100, -6 at y=-150).

deck.note: seam = where the surface first rises above z = +2 toward the band; notch_* = notch open edge. Rear closure = arch.edge_by_x; front closure behind the notch = notch.back_edge_by_x.

clock.source: texture (bright chrome/dial ring, circle fit) + height
clock.note: nearly flush in the scan (~1 mm); glass/chrome can make LiDAR heights unreliable

cup_ring.source: texture (chrome) circle fit; heights from the top-view height map
cup_ring.note: cup inner wall appears conical (scanner cannot see steep deep walls); floor level approximate

socket_plate.source: height map edges at half height (z = 2.25)

slot_surround.note: slot opening is not captured (filled over by the scanner); centre x uncertain by about 2 mm

slices.note: chains from slicing the aligned mesh, resampled every 10 mm, only pieces >= 15 mm long; z = -3 replaces z = 0 (the deck surface itself lies at 0). Lower slices are fragmentary.

qi_pad.note: position = where it lay on the table: near edge about 60 mm and centre about 150 mm in front of the arm tips; not a fitted position

plug.note: cigarette plug lying on the table with its cable mostly lost; length includes the right-angle exit

thin cables (only two short pieces captured in the notch)
